opening_message:
Ticket 1: Dominic Taylor (employee ID E004) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E004.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Dominic Taylor (E004) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Source Code is within policy (write allowed for full-time employees; Engineer owns Source Code). Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E004 (Dominic Taylor) as a contractor with basic security training, which differs from the earlier note's full_time entry. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training limits to read; requested write exceeds policy, so recommend read.
reason: There is a direct conflict between the two notes on employment type: HR reports E004 (Dominic Taylor) as full_time, while the Security agent (who looked up the employee in their own database) reports contractor with basic security training and explicitly flags the discrepancy. Under the access policy, a contractor with basic training may have at most read. Since the requested write exceeds that maximum, the maximum level (read) is granted. Granting read is also the least-privilege-safe level given the unresolved conflict.
